fatal_errors: The proposed oxide dispersion is neither present nor introduced in the described Al-Cr-Fe-Ni multilayers.
The governing modulation-period/interface-coherency variable is omitted.
High-temperature bulk-creep conditions are invented, whereas the target concerns room-temperature nanoindentation creep.
The uncoated substrate is an inappropriate baseline for distinguishing coherent, semicoherent, and grain-boundary-dominated coatings.
No supporting prior evidence is supplied.
The predicted 30% improvement is inconsistent with the factor-of-two falsification threshold.
explanation: The hypothesis only aligns at the broad level of dislocation-controlled creep resistance in an FCC/BCC coating. It does not reconstruct the controlled variation in multilayer period, the semicoherent-interface optimum at 16 nm, misfit-dislocation pileup, proposed stress-induced interfacial amorphization, or the transition toward diffusion/interface-slip creep. Its 800 °C, 200 MPa, 100 h conditions and oxide-dispersion mechanism are unsupported extrapolations outside the established room-temperature, 5 mN nanoindentation regime. A with/without-oxide comparison is nominally testable, but oxide content is not operationally manipulated, the stated intervention is characterization rather than materials processing, and the baseline and falsification threshold are poorly matched to the prediction.
